newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Schroeder wants decision on coalition.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Schroeder wants decision on coalition.

text.p: The man who polls say is most likely to oust German Chancellor Helmut Kohl next year said on Wednesday his Social Democrats (SPD) should commit themselves before the election to a coalition with the environmentalist Greens.

Gerhard Schroeder, premier of Lower Saxony state, said in an interview with Stern magazine that voters wanted the SPD to state its preference before the election rather than remain uncommitted as in past losing efforts.

"The voters won't accept it if we dodge the issue and tell them we will decide after the election what our coalition preferences are," Schroeder said, according to a text of the interview released ahead of Thursday's edition.

Schroeder said the SPD should aim for a leftist coalition with the Greens if the parties secured a majority, but that it should remain open to the possibility of a "grand coalition" with Kohl's Christian Democrats if the election result made this necessary.
"The preference for SPD-Greens should not become dogmatic," he said. "Other solutions should be possible."

Schroeder said there were many leaders in Kohl's CDU with whom the SPD could work together, such as Saxony state premier Kurt Biedenkopf, Defence Minister Volker Ruehe and Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann.
Most opinion polls suggest that the pragmatic and pro-business Schroeder would defeat Kohl if voters were asked to elect the chancellor directly.
SPD chairman Oskar Lafontaine, who was defeated by Kohl in 1990, is the other leading SPD candidate to spearhead the 1998 election bid.
Although Kohl has already said he will run again, the SPD has refused to yield to pressure to decide on a chancellor candidate before next year.
Schroeder said that "the candidate who maximises the chances of the SPD" would lead the party into the election.
